newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper weakens early, shrugs off stock drop.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper weakens early, shrugs off stock drop.

text.p: COMEX copper weakened in early trading despite a healthy draw in LME stocks overnight and a widening in the London backwardation.

"I think this appears to be an attempt to find some downside stops to flush out some of the longs. It goes against current nearby fundamentals where you can expect a 3,000 to 5,000 tonne draw in LME stocks next week," Malcolm Freeman of GNI Ltd said.
At 0944 EDT, July COMEX was off 0.45 cent at 121.70 cents a lb, traded 122.60 to 121.30 cents. Spot June was down 0.60 cent at 121.40 cents.
LME stocks fell 1,800 tonnes Friday to 121,550 tonnes.

The London cash to three months backwardation which has helped and underpinned the recent advance in red metal tags to 13-month highs, strengthened Friday to $128/$135, up from $115/$120 by COMEX close Thursday.
Meanwhile Inco Ltd said late Thursday that talks with union leaders representing striking employees at the company's Sudbury mining operations, had reached a criticial stage.
Union officials insisted the talks had broken off and the strike, begun June 2, continued.
Inco, the world's biggest nickel seller, is also a supplier of copper to the Northeastern region of U.S.
